intro: Agents took the week. Anthropic launched Claude Duet and gave Agent Skills to an open foundation, while AI security tools found critical flaws in PHP and Brotli. A poisoned LiteLLM release showed the other side of the agent supply chain.

top.title: Anthropic launches Claude Duet, an always-on background agent
top.body: Claude Duet is a proactive agent that runs on its own cloud computer and keeps working after the app closes. It runs on Claude Opus 5.5, shares memories, skills, connectors and plugins with Claude, and asks before it sends messages, pays, signs or deletes.

top.title: Anthropic donates Agent Skills to the Agentic AI Foundation
top.body: Anthropic gave the Agent Skills standard, name, logo, GitHub organization and agentskills.io domain to the Agentic AI Foundation under the Linux Foundation, which already hosts MCP. Engineers from Anthropic, Google, OpenAI and other companies will maintain it.

top.title: OpenAI cuts live internet from frontier training, builds offline web
top.body: OpenAI said it removed live internet access for all frontier models during training. Models now browse and search a large indexed, cached copy of the web.

top.title: AI uncovers PHP2Shell: unauthenticated RCE in PHP core
top.body: Wiz disclosed four bugs under CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, with CVSS up to 9.2. The flaws allow unauthenticated remote code execution and memory disclosure, and Wiz showed RCE on current WordPress, Drupal and Joomla images.

top.title: OpenAI red-team agents find unauthenticated RCE in Brotli
top.body: OpenAI said its red-teaming exercise found a flaw in the Brotli compression library that allows unauthenticated remote code execution. Brotli is included in Node.js, Bun and Envoy.

top.title: Poisoned LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI steals credentials and installs backdoor
top.body: All seven LiteLLM 1.107.0 wheels on PyPI and the v1.107.0, latest, main-latest and main-stable Docker images carried malware on 21 October between about 11:39 and 14:20 UTC. A .pth stealer ran in every Python process and took SSH keys, cloud credentials, CI secrets and LLM keys; a sitecustomize.py backdoor fetched more code every hour.

top.title: DeepSeek open-sources DeepInfer, its production inference engine
top.body: DeepSeek released DeepInfer under the Apache 2.0 license. It powers DeepSeek's production services and supports DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on NVIDIA SM100 GPUs and Huawei Ascend 950 NPUs.

top.title: Moonshot launches Kimi K3.1 Pro, close to Opus 5.5 on coding
top.body: Moonshot AI launched Kimi K3.1 Pro on October 23 on its paid cloud services. It is a post-trained upgrade of Kimi K3, a 3-trillion-parameter mixture-of-experts model that activates 16 of 896 experts at a time.

top.title: Claude Models launch on Google Cloud as an Anthropic-managed service
top.body: Anthropic launched Claude Models on Google Cloud (Anthropic managed). Google Cloud IAM controls access and Google Cloud Marketplace handles billing.

top.title: Claude traces NIST ECDSA curve seeds to a 1990s random generator
top.body: An Anthropic internal research model found that the seeds for P-192, P-224, P-256, P-384 and P-521 came from lrand48 seeded with Unix timestamps from 1997 and 1998. It recovered generator states by brute force and LLL lattice reduction.

models.name: Kimi K3.1 Pro
models.what: Kimi K3.1 Pro is a 2.8T-parameter MoE model with 104B active parameters and a 1M-token context, priced at $2 input and $10 output per million tokens.

models.name: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
models.what: MiniMax put MiniMax-M3.1-Flash weights on Hugging Face under the minimax-community license.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1-Flash-1017
models.what: DeepSeek released a minor update to V4.1-Flash under the MIT license with a 1M-token context.

models.name: Voxtral 3
models.what: Voxtral 3 includes Small Transcribe 3 ($0.004/min), Mini Transcribe 3 (4B, $0.0035/min), Mini Transcribe Realtime 3 ($0.008/min, under 500 ms) and a TTS model ($13 per 1M characters) with voice cloning.

models.name: Timestral
models.what: Mistral released Timestral, four time-series foundation models with 5M to 209M parameters, under a modified MIT license.

chips.title: NVIDIA Minerva brings end-to-end observability to AI factories
chips.body: Minerva joins telemetry from NVIDIA GPUs, networking, storage, schedulers and jobs into a live knowledge graph of GPUs, SuperNICs, switches, cables and jobs.

chips.title: NVIDIA OpenShell: policy-enforced sandbox runtime for agent fleets
chips.body: OpenShell runs each agent in an isolated sandbox with kernel controls on files and system calls, and checks every network connection against policy.

chips.title: Deep Fusion Memory adds parametric knowledge without online retrieval
chips.body: Deep Fusion Memory predicts a chunk-level memory from preceding context and fuses it into hidden states through gated cross-attention, with the backbone frozen.

An MCP server that makes background music and sound effects locally for Claude Code and other MCP clients.
A read-only MCP server that lets an agent search and read your own WhatsApp messages.

skill_of_week.name: single-agent-loop-kit
skill_of_week.what: A Claude Code skill and reference loop from Anthropic that moves a multi-agent system (a router plus subagents) to one agent loop that loads skills and tools on demand. It works in three steps: measure the current system with an eval, combine subagents that always run together, then fold the rest into skills one at a time and keep each change only if the scores hold.
skill_of_week.verdict: Worth a try if you run multi-agent setups
skill_of_week.note: Honest take: the idea is strong and it comes with an offline smoke test that costs nothing. But the repo is a reference, not a product: Anthropic does not maintain it, it has had only two real test runs, and real eval runs cost model tokens. Use it to structure a migration, not as a finished tool.
